title: ⚛️ React useEffect — How Does It Work?
excerpt: For example, fetching data, setting up timers, or listening for browser events.
body:
ㅤ
📘 Engineering Notes | From Concepts to Code — Post 14
ㅤ
When building React applications, we often need to perform operations outside the normal rendering process.

For example, fetching data, setting up timers, or listening for browser events.

That's where useEffect comes in! 🚀

Let's understand it with simple examples. 👇
ㅤ
1️⃣ 𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗜𝘀 𝘂𝘀𝗲𝗘𝗳𝗳𝗲𝗰𝘁? 🔄

useEffect is a React Hook that helps synchronize a component with external systems.

It runs after React commits updates to the UI.

Example:

useEffect(() => {
  document.title = "My React App";
}, []);

This updates the browser tab title when the component mounts.
ㅤ
2️⃣ 𝗨𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗿𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗻𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗗𝗲𝗽𝗲𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗻𝗰𝘆 𝗔𝗿𝗿𝗮𝘆 📦

The dependency array controls when the Effect needs to run again.

🔹 No dependency array
Runs after every committed render.

🔹 Empty array []
Runs on mount, with an extra development check possible in Strict Mode.

🔹 [userId]
Runs on mount and when userId changes.
ㅤ
3️⃣ 𝗥𝗲𝗮𝗹-𝗪𝗼𝗿𝗹𝗱 𝗘𝘅𝗮𝗺𝗽𝗹𝗲 — 𝗧𝗶𝗺𝗲𝗿 ⏱️

Imagine displaying a timer in a dashboard.

useEffect(() => {
  const timer = setInterval(() => {
    console.log("Tick");
  }, 1000);

  return () => clearInterval(timer);
}, []);

The Effect starts a timer, and the cleanup function clears it when needed.
ㅤ
4️⃣ 𝗪𝗵𝘆 𝗜𝘀 𝗖𝗹𝗲𝗮𝗻𝘂𝗽 𝗜𝗺𝗽𝗼𝗿𝘁𝗮𝗻𝘁? 🧹

Effects may set up subscriptions, timers, or event listeners.

Without proper cleanup, these can continue running unnecessarily.

✅ Clear timers
✅ Remove event listeners
✅ Disconnect subscriptions
✅ Cancel or ignore outdated requests
ㅤ
5️⃣ 𝗖𝗼𝗺𝗺𝗼𝗻 𝘂𝘀𝗲𝗘𝗳𝗳𝗲𝗰𝘁 𝗠𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗸𝗲𝘀 ⚠️

❌ Missing required dependencies
❌ Forgetting cleanup
❌ Using Effects for simple calculations
❌ Creating unnecessary update loops

💡 If a value can be calculated directly from props or state during rendering, you often don't need useEffect.
ㅤ
💡 𝗠𝘆 𝗞𝗲𝘆 𝗧𝗮𝗸𝗲𝗮𝘄𝗮𝘆

useEffect isn't just a way to run code after rendering.

Its main purpose is to synchronize React components with external systems.

Understanding dependencies and cleanup helps us build more predictable and maintainable applications.

🚀 Use Effects when needed, not for everything.
